register.name: El Tortuguero–La Esperanza Rural Electricity Transmission Project
register.detail: OPEC Fund · public-sector loan · approved 15 April 2020 · signed 21 July 2020 · total project cost $23M · ongoing
register.note: Grid connections for about 300,000 people in the southern Caribbean coast region
register.text: An OPEC Fund loan to the Republic of Nicaragua to extend transmission infrastructure and grid connections to remote communities in the southern Caribbean coastal region. It brings electricity to homes that have none and serves the energy standard, where 88.7% of Nicaraguans have electricity.

register.name: Programme for the Improvement and Expansion of Four Drinking Water Systems in Five Cities
register.detail: CABEI · approved 25 September 2024 · loan contract 2338 signed 4 and 10 March 2025 · approved by the National Assembly 2 April 2025 · Tranche A $85.6M from CABEI ordinary resources, Tranche B $44.4M · executed by ENACAL
register.note: More than 140,000 Nicaraguans expected to benefit by 2026
register.text: A CABEI loan to the Republic of Nicaragua to expand and improve the drinking water systems of Ocotal, Camoapa, Diriamba, San Jorge and Buenos Aires, with 26 new supply sources, more than 11,700 household connections installed or rehabilitated and more than 27 million cubic metres of drinking water a year. It serves the water standard directly, for which no WHO/UNICEF measure is published for Nicaragua.

register.name: National Sustainable Electrification and Renewable Energy Programme (PNESER), Tranche A
register.detail: CABEI · completion announced 10 February 2025 · executed by ENATREL with the Ministry of Energy and Mines · Tranches B and C under way
register.note: 806 communities connected to the grid, serving 30,731 homes and 161,664 people
register.text: CABEI financing for the first tranche of Nicaragua’s national programme for sustainable electrification and renewable energy, which connected 806 communities to the grid, regularised a legal and safe supply for 28,322 households and built 379.2 km of new network and a 75 km, 230 kV transmission line. It served the energy standard for more than 336,000 Nicaraguans.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 28.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: CacaoNica
items.text: A cocoa cooperative in Waslala, in the North Caribbean Coast Autonomous Region, founded by 69 smallholder farmers 25 years ago and now of 372 members, that exports Rainforest Alliance–certified cocoa to Europe, earning its members $1.20 a pound.

items.name: SOPPEXCCA
items.text: A union of coffee cooperatives in Jinotega that sells only the coffee of its 405 member producers, among them the women behind its Las Hermanas coffee, and makes small loans to young women to start businesses.

items.name: Fundenuse
items.text: A microfinance institution, financed by Oikocredit since 2004, that offers loans and technical assistance to micro-entrepreneurs, many of them women, and farmers in northern and central Nicaragua, with 22,906 clients, 55.2% of them women and 65.6% rural.

items.name: PRODESA
items.text: A microfinance institution based in Juigalpa that lends to smallholder and mid-sized farmers and entrepreneurs in six regions of Nicaragua’s remote Atlantic area, where many people have no basic financial services, with 21,433 active borrowers, 49.1% of them women.

items.name: MiCrédito
items.text: A microfinance institution that uses Oikocredit finance to extend loans to new clients and aims to lead in financial products for rural areas, with 11,988 clients, 59.3% of them women.
